import pandas as pd

def main():
    # File paths for the source CSV files
    source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/test_0.csv"
    source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/test_1.csv"
    target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_42/target_multisource_cot.csv"

    # Load Source 0: user ratings data
    # Schema: ['user_id', 'item_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']
    df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path)
    # Ensure correct dtypes
    df_source0 = df_source0.astype({
        'user_id': 'int32',
        'item_id': 'int32',
        'rating': 'int8',
        'timestamp': 'int64'
    })

    # Load Source 1: movie metadata
    # Schema includes 'item_id', 'movie title', and many other columns
    df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path)
    # Ensure item_id is int for join
    df_source1['item_id'] = df_source1['item_id'].astype('int32')
    # 'movie title' is string, no conversion needed

    # Join Source 0 and Source 1 on 'item_id' to get movie titles for each rating
    # This is a left join because we want to keep all ratings, even if some movies might be missing metadata
    df_merged = pd.merge(df_source0, df_source1[['item_id', 'movie title']], on='item_id', how='left')

    # According to target schema:
    # ['user_id': integer, 'item_id': integer, 'rating': integer, 'timestamp': integer, 'movie title': string]
    # We already have these columns after merge.

    # Check for any missing movie titles after join and fill with empty string or a placeholder
    df_merged['movie title'] = df_merged['movie title'].fillna('')

    # Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
    df_target = df_merged[['user_id', 'item_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'movie title']]

    # Save the transformed data to the target CSV file
    df_target.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
